summary: Feed s135_double to APM is degraded: 24.2% duplicates and 2.3% TCP packet loss detected. Duplicates waste APM capacity and skew metrics; drops cause incomplete transactions.

findings.root_cause: Same packets delivered twice to the tool, most likely from aggregating two SPAN/mirror feeds or a TAP/SPAN overlap without broker deduplication, or a loop in the packet broker aggregation. 658 of 2714 packets (24.2%) exceed 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will count duplicate transactions, inflate latency/throughput metrics, create false retransmission signals, and waste 24% of its 10Gbps processing capacity on redundant data.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication at egress to APM to suppress identical packets arriving within a short window before delivery, eliminating double-counting without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN buffer overflow/congestion causing intermittent drops. TCP sequence gaps show 57 of 2511 TCP packets (2.3%) missing, above 1% threshold, while tool itself is not overloaded, pointing to loss in the visibility fabric before the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM sees incomplete flows and missing segments, leading to broken transaction traces, inaccurate latency/error rates, and missed application performance degradations due to 2.3% data loss.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across additional APM instances/ports or filter/slice unwanted traffic at the broker to reduce oversubscription and buffer drops; APM does not need full payload so slicing is also an option to lower bandwidth while preserving headers.
